title: Quicksilver AI onramp: hosted vs private constraints discussion
summary: Intro discovery for a small AI startup deciding between Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private. Focus on fastest time-to-first-token, free credits for proof-of-concept, data residency and VPC constraints, and cost/latency tradeoffs. SE walked through quickstart flow and typical pilot sizing. Next steps: send credit link, quickstart checklist, and proposed pilot pricing + dedicated sizing doc.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Maya: share free credits link + quickstart checklist by 2025-06-24
Carlos: attach dedicated sizing template and sample perf numbers by 2025-06-25
Quicksilver: confirm pilot workload sample and preferred region by 2025-06-27
Schedule a 60-min technical demo/canary planning session week of 2025-06-30
action_items: Maya - Send invoice-free credits link and summary of hosted getting started steps (due 2025-06-24)
Carlos - Provide rough GPU pool sizing for 50 RPS 1k tokens/session P50 300ms target (due 2025-06-25)
Leah - Share security contact and compliance checklist items for SOC2 scope (due 2025-06-27)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, account lead. Carlos, our solutions engineer, is here too.
[00:08] Leah: Hi Maya, hi Carlos, this is Leah. We just wanted to run through options — we're trying to get something up quick and also understand security for enterprise customers.
[00:15] Carlos: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — quickstart / free credits, demo of API flow, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and then Q&A. Is that okay?
[00:23] Daniel: Yep sounds good. I'm Daniel, ML engineer. Main thing: time-to-first-token, we want to reduce friction for our product team to build an assistant by next sprint.
[00:30] Omar: Omar here, infra. We'll be evaluating VPC, KMS, and data retention needs.
[00:36] Maya: Cool. Two quick notes: our PLG path is designed so you can sign up, get free credits, and be calling the API in less than an hour. Typical time-to-first-token is 10-20 minutes if you follow the quickstart.
[00:48] Leah: Ten minutes? That would be ideal. But is that true when you enable VPC/private?
[00:53] Maya: Good question. Hosted (the default) is the fastest: you sign up, SDK key, call endpoints. Dedicated and Private require some setup — dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud and takes a day to wire up once the contract is accepted and capacity is allocated; private (VPC or on-prem) depends on network approvals and can take a couple weeks.
[01:10] Daniel: So for immediate dev we should go hosted, then transition to private for production?
[01:15] Carlos: That's a common pattern. Start hosted for POC and iterate on prompts. For production, if you need data residency or VPC egress, move to dedicated or private. Our routing makes the API call identical so your code doesn't change, just the model id and endpoint.
[01:27] Omar: We have regulatory customers asking for no egress to public internet and KMS-managed keys. How does Redwood handle that?
[01:34] Carlos: For VPC/private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and have an on-prem package. For dedicated in cloud, we integrate with customer KMS via a managed connector, and audit logs are retained. We also support SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[01:45] Leah: Is Redwood SOC2? We need SOC2 and ISO 27001.
[01:49] Maya: Yes, we're SOC2 Type II. ISO is on roadmap and we can share the current security pack. I'll attach those docs.
[01:57] Daniel: Great. On the dev side — what does the quickstart look like? Is there an SDK snippet?
[02:02] Carlos: Yup. The quickstart is a 3-step: sign up, create API key, call the text-generation or chat endpoint. We'll show the SDK snippet now — pseudo transcript: "import redwood; client = Redwood(api_key='...'); resp = client.chat.create(model='rw1-large', messages=[...])". Most teams have their first token within 10-20 min.
[02:20] Leah: Do you have pre-built integrations for Next.js or Vercel?
[02:24] Maya: We have example templates and a Vercel serverless demo repo. Also a NextJS client-side pattern with server middleware to keep the API key secret.
[02:31] Omar: About cost — what is the unit economics for dev and for production? We have a small team and cost matters.
[02:37] Maya: Hosted pricing is usage-based per token — dev costs are usually trivial for POC with credits. For production, dedicated gives predictable monthly cost (reserved GPU pools) and you get a cost per million token estimate. Our Optimize tooling suggests batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost.
[02:51] Daniel: Can you estimate price for a 50 RPS workload with average 1k tokens/session and 300ms P50?
[02:58] Carlos: Rough back-of-envelope: with a 1k token session, you want batching and maybe fp16/4-bit quant on compatible models. For 50 RPS sustained that's non-trivial — you'd look at several GPUs; I'll pull a sizing doc for that.
[03:10] Maya: We'll put together a dedicated sizing and a pilot cost outline.
[03:14] Leah: For the POC, is there a way to lock the model version and avoid silent regresses?
[03:19] Carlos: Yes — model pinning and versioning are first-class. You can pin to a verified model hash and also configure rollouts/canaries. We also have eval hooks so you can run prompt sets and watch regressions.
[03:31] Daniel: Nice. Any gotchas with prefix caching and session state for chat?
[03:36] Carlos: We support KV cache and automatic prefix caching. Sometimes we see mis- configs where the cache TTL is too short or the tokenization mismatch causes hit misses — easy to debug with tracing in the console.
[03:46] Omar: Can we see logs for individual tokens? We need auditability.
[03:50] Carlos: We have token-level cost and latency breakdowns and request traces. For private setups, logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint and we can integrate with SIEM.
[04:00] Leah: Ok, can we step through a hypothetical onboarding flow? Say we want to be calling by tomorrow in hosted.
[04:07] Maya: Steps: 1) Sign up and verify domain; 2) Create org and team; 3) Request free credits (I can provision); 4) Create API key in console; 5) Run quickstart sample with SDK; 6) Share sample prompts to set Eval monitors. If you start now you could get to alpha today.
[04:22] Daniel: When you say free credits — any limits on models or throughput?
[04:26] Maya: Credits are typically unrestricted across our model catalog but we may limit sustained throughput. For benchmarks or heavy testing we request you coordinate so we can allocate capacity.
[04:35] Omar: Does the credit use show up in billing? We want to keep POC separate from org billing.
[04:40] Maya: Credits are tracked separately on the account and don't produce invoices. We can also create a sandbox org for your team.
[04:46] Leah: Good. On compliance: will Redwood sign an addendum for data residency and deletion?
[04:51] Maya: Yes, we have data processing addendums and deletion APIs. For private deployments you can also keep data on-prem.
[04:57] Daniel: I'm curious about model selection — do you host open models only or proprietary ones too?
[05:02] Carlos: We host curated open models and also some verified performance profiles; we don't currently host closed-source proprietary models. We also provide guidance on quantization and kernel selection per workload.
[05:12] Leah: Can the team try a small benchmark? We want to compare latency against our current OpenAI calls.
[05:17] Carlos: Sure. If you share a small prompt set and target region, we can run a perf bench on hosted and on a dedicated sizing and send results. Note: differences in batching and seq length matter a lot.
[05:29] Omar: Our infra team needs to know about VPC peering, egress cost, and whether we need to open ports.
[05:35] Carlos: For VPC private deployments we use an ENI or customer VPN tunnel. Egress is fully contained in the VPC. For dedicated in cloud there is usually a managed connector with restricted egress. We'll share an infra checklist.
[05:47] Leah: What are typical SLAs for dedicated?
[05:51] Maya: We offer SLA-backed latency and uptime for dedicated customers — 99.9% depending on contract. Hosted service has a different tiered SLA but for PLG it's best-effort, then you upgrade to dedicated for mission-critical.
[06:02] Daniel: Any friction for auth — rotate keys, per-route tokens?
[06:06] Carlos: We support short-lived tokens via session tokens and also per-route keys. Key rotation is in the console and via API.
[06:13] Leah: Ok what about rate limits — do they throttle or queue? We want predictable behavior.
[06:18] Maya: We have quotas per org and rate limiting. Dedicated can be provisioned to meet your expected RPS and we have burst behavior configured.
[06:27] Omar: If we prototype on hosted and then switch to dedicated, does data move automatically?
[06:31] Carlos: Data is segregated; for model artifacts and logs we can export and ingest into dedicated/private. There's a migration playbook; the API surface remains the same so integration effort is minimal.
[06:42] Maya: Any other constraints we should know about?
[06:45] Leah: One more — we run some on-device pre- and post-processing. Does Redwood provide client-side SDKs?
[06:51] Carlos: We have Python, Node, and Java SDKs. Client-side patterns recommended are server middleware proxies for keys. For on-device, you can run local models and call Redwood for large-context generations if wanted.
[07:02] Daniel: Could you show a short live quickstart in 2-3 steps?
[07:06] Carlos: Sure. I'll narrate: sign up, create API key, sample curl: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"rw1-medium","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize latest sales deck"}]}'
[07:25] Daniel: Looks straightforward. Any gotchas with tokenization differences?
[07:28] Carlos: Tokenization varies by model family; we document tokenizer and provide token counters in the console. Some models do sub-tokenization different from GPT; it's usually fine but watch accounting across your pipeline.
[07:40] Leah: For the pilot success criteria we want: 1) integration within 1 sprint, 2) mean latency <500ms P50 and <900ms P95 for chat, 3) cost target sub-$0.01 per session. Is that realistic?
[07:52] Carlos: We can aim for that. 500ms P50 is reasonable with the right model and dedicated capacity; cost depends on tokens and batching. We'll run numbers.
[08:02] Omar: Anything about egress billing from the cloud provider when on dedicated?
[08:07] Carlos: Egress between provider regions can incur cloud provider egress charges; we'll help you estimate and provide guidance to colocate in the same region.
[08:16] Maya: Quick recap: you want to POC on hosted now to move fast; evaluate latency and integration; then plan a pilot on dedicated or private for production with KMS and VPC. We'll provide credits, quickstart links, infra checklist, and sizing doc.
[08:29] Leah: Sounds good. Who will be the point of contact on your side for technical details?
[08:33] Maya: Carlos will be primary SE; I'll be your AE. I'll send a calendar invite for the next tech deep dive.
[08:40] Daniel: One more question — do you have pre-built prompt templates for customer support assistants?
[08:44] Carlos: Yes — we have a prompt library and some starter evaluation sets. We'll include examples in the quickstart repo.
[08:51] Omar: Could we get sample logs for audit review?
[08:54] Maya: Yes, sample sanitized logs and compliance docs will be attached.
[08:58] Leah: Thank you. Any blockers from our side? We'll gather prompt set and security contact.
[09:03] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[09:06] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional auto-caption errors (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash"), speaker labels sometimes align to role rather than person. Some filler words removed for readability.
